title: Bin El Ouidane reservoir, 4 Jul to 8 Oct 2026
summary: Between 4 Jul and 8 Oct 2026 the lake went from 31.86 km2 to 29.91 km2, while the whole circle got brighter, with mean HH up 1.69 dB. The 8 Oct date carries two flags, so the brightening should not be read as change on the ground.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.text: Over 96 days the lake changed by -1.95 km2, or -6.1%. HH turned brighter by more than 3 dB on 40.54 km2 and darker on only 0.11 km2. HV turned brighter on 7.29 km2, and mean HV rose by 0.73 dB.

sections.heading: Where, by terrain type
sections.text: The brightening covers every type. Rough dry ground and fields had 19.12 km2 brighter in HH and rose 2.54 dB, and trees, shrub and rugged slopes had 10.44 km2 brighter. Built-up land, which should stay stable, rose 2.35 dB in HH, and the open water type rose 2.19 dB.

sections.heading: Possible causes
sections.text: Possible cause: a processing offset in the 8 Oct product, since buildings brightened like fields; reprocessed files would settle it. Possible cause: a wet surface after rain; rain records for early October would check it. Possible cause for the lake: summer drawdown; the dam's level records would confirm it.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: 8 Oct 2026 carries two flags: the lake water threshold moved more than 1.0 dB from the previous date, and backscatter over built-up land shifted more than 0.5 dB from its June-September median. NASA has no NISAR data from 27 Jul to 10 Aug 2026, so nothing between 16 Jul and 21 Aug 2026 is seen. Lake areas are approximate.

sections.heading: What an agency could do next
sections.text: Use an unflagged end date for a firm lake figure, and check October rain records before reading any land change here.
